unlock_procedure: 1. Provide a credential the helper can use without a dialog: a fine-grained PAT with 'Contents: read and write' on the target repository, exported as GITHUB_TOKEN for the session (never written into the repository).
2. Alternative A: `gh auth login` (the gh CLI is not installed on this machine) and push through gh's credential helper.
3. Alternative B: an SSH remote (`git remote set-url origin git@github.com:<owner>/<repo>.git`) with a key already trusted by the account.
4. Alternative C: `git -c credential.helper=store` plus a git-credentials file created outside the repository, removed after the push.
5. Push the branch: `git push -u origin agent/edge-recovery/WP-EDGE-00-baseline` (the lane branch carries all WP-EDGE-01/02/03 commits).
6. Verify with an anonymous read: `git ls-remote --heads origin 'refs/heads/agent/edge-recovery/*'` must show the ref and its sha.
7. Confirm the pushed head equals the local head: `git rev-parse HEAD` against the sha the step-6 listing shows.
8. Do not push tags or force anything; the lane history is append-only.
9. Record the push exit code and the verified sha in this file, replacing BLOCKED_GITHUB_AUTH with the observed result.

limitations: The forward window is short by construction: 2 new independent days since the freeze, 226 counting the frozen prefix. The lane reports the count and reads no admission criterion.
Every PnL figure in this record is hypothetical (hypothetical: true, order_sent: false). No capital, no order, no private endpoint anywhere in the lane.
Risk parity compares two implementations on identical inputs; it says nothing about which limits are right.
The intraday arms read BTC's 1h series as context, exactly as the frozen campaign did, extended with the forward 1h bars so the context covers the window.
The lane depends on public Binance REST; when no bar has closed it records no_new_data and adds nothing (exercised for real in this session).

ruff format --check is not green on the lane's files (8 of 9) and ruff check . reports 150 findings elsewhere in the repo under the locally installed ruff 0.15.20; both are pre-existing toolchain/repo debt, measured and published, not fixed here.

The repository-wide pytest run reports 15 failures, none of them in this lane: they belong to other lanes and to the host state of this shared checkout (disk at 97% makes WP-9's disk preflight refuse, and other lanes' state views drifted). They are measured and published here, not fixed, because fixing them would mean touching work that is not this package's.
